## What Changed

`src/dedupe.js` — replaced the O(n²) `out.some(...)` scan with a `Set` of normalized keys:

```js
const seen = new Set()
for (const record of records) {
  const key = record.email.trim().toLowerCase()
  if (!seen.has(key)) {
    seen.add(key)
    out.push(record)
  }
}
```

Return behavior is unchanged: first record per trimmed, case-insensitive email is kept, in original order, as the same object references.

## Evidence

- Equivalence check against the original implementation on randomized inputs (n = 0, 1, 10, 500, 2000): identical lengths, order, and object references.
- Edge case with mixed-case/whitespace emails: first occurrence preserved.
- Benchmark, 12,000 records, 20 runs after warmup: **median 0.425 ms, max 0.523 ms** (well under 300 ms).

## Why

The original rescanned every already-kept record and re-normalized its email on each comparison, so cost grew quadratically. A hash-set membership check makes each record O(1) on average, with the same normalization and first-wins semantics.

  if (text.length <= n) return text
  if (n <= 0) return ""
  return text.slice(0, n - 1) + "…"
}
```

## What Changed

**`src/store.js`**
- Added a monotonic `version` counter incremented synchronously on every `set`, exposed as `db.version()`.
- Existing `all()`/`set()`/`loads()` behavior is unchanged.

**`src/settings.js`**
- Cached entries now record the store version. A cache entry is only used if it matches the current version and is under the 60s TTL, so any save invalidates immediately.
- Added single-flight loading: concurrent `getSettings()` calls on a cold cache share one in-flight promise, so the store is hit once.
- `loadSettings()` snapshots the version before `db.all()` and re-checks it after the await. If a save occurred during the load, the stale snapshot is discarded and the load retries, so it can never repopulate the cache with pre-save data.

## Evidence

Temporary harness covering the required behaviors (removed afterward):

```

ok: cold-cache burst loads once
ok: in-flight save does not resurrect old value

ok: post-save burst loads once

```

Session verdict: verified.
```

## Why

Invalidation lives in the store rather than only in `saveSetting`, so any write path — including a direct `db.set` — advances the version. Version checks around the slow load close the race where a load started before a save finishes after it. Sharing the in-flight promise is what collapses a cold-cache burst into a single store read while still allowing that shared load to retry if it was invalidated mid-flight.
